{{Tooltip|W|Won}} 53–41 vs. [[2010–11 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]] }} {{2010–11 Big East men's basketball standings}} [[File:UConn Men's Basketball 2011 Championship Parade (5630693895).jpg|thumb|Players and coaches, joined by Connecticut Governor [[Dannel Malloy]] and Lieutenant Governor [[Nancy Wyman]], pose with the championship trophy]] The '''2010–11 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Connecticut]] in the 2010–2011 [[NCAA Division I]] basketball season. The Huskies were coached by [[Jim Calhoun]] and played their home games at the [[XL Center]] in [[Hartford, Connecticut]], and on campus at the [[Harry A. Gampel Pavilion]] in [[Storrs, Connecticut]]. The Huskies were a member of the [[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|Big East Conference]]. The Huskies entered the year unranked and picked to finish tenth in the Big East. In November, they won the [[Maui Invitational Tournament]] for the second time. They finished the Big East regular season in a tie for ninth place at 9–9. Led by [[Kemba Walker]] who scored a tournament record 130 points, they became the first school to win five conference tournament games in as many days in claiming their seventh [[Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament title]]. By winning the tournament, they were awarded an automatic berth into the [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. They advanced to their fourth Final Four with a 65–63 victory over [[2010–11 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] and advanced to their third national championship game with a 56–55 victory over [[2010-11 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] and beat [[2010-11 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]] 53–41 for their first championship since [[2004 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|2004]] and third since [[1999 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|1999]]. ==Before the season== The Huskies were coming off of a tumultuous [[2009–10 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|2009–10]] season in which they failed to earn a berth in the [[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] for the second time in four years, and amidst an NCAA investigation into alleged recruiting violations involving Nate Miles. As a result of the investigation, assistant coaches Patrick Sellers and [[Beau Archibald]] resigned from their positions.{{cite news|last=Anthony|first=Mike|title=UConn Assistants Sellers, Archibald Out In Light Of NCAA Violations|url=https://www.courant.com/2010/05/28/uconn-assistants-sellers-archibald-out-in-light-of-ncaa-violations/|access-date=May 15, 2011|newspaper=Hartford Courant|date=May 28, 2010}} Later that summer, [[Kevin Ollie]] was hired to take Sellers' role as assistant coach,{{cite news|last=Katz|first=Andy|title=Ollie says he's joining UConn's staff|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=5348090|access-date=May 15, 2011|publisher=ESPN|date=July 2, 2010}} and [[Glen Miller (basketball)|Glen Miller]] was brought on as Director of Basketball Operations, replacing Archibald.{{cite news|last=Divver|first=Mark|title=UConn adds former Brown coach Glen Miller to staff|url=http://hoopsblog.projo.com/2010/07/uconn-adds-form.html|access-date=May 15, 2011|newspaper=The Providence Journal|date=July 2, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110818010245/http://hoopsblog.projo.com/2010/07/uconn-adds-form.html|archive-date=August 18, 2011|url-status=dead}} Both men have previous links with Jim Calhoun. Ollie played for the Huskies under Calhoun from 1991 to 1995, while Miller was an assistant coach under Calhoun from 1986 until 1992.
In addition to the coaching changes, the Huskies also needed to replace three graduating starters: Jerome Dyson, [[Stanley Robinson (basketball)|Stanley Robinson]] and Gavin Edwards. Reserve forward [[Ater Majok]] also left the school before the season began.{{cite news|last=O'Neil|first=Dana|title=Majok gives UConn more bad news|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/14819/majoks-departure-more-bad-news-for-uconn|access-date=May 15, 2011|publisher=ESPN|date=September 1, 2010}}

LaFleur *[[Kevin Ollie]]}} == Regular season == After a pair of exhibition games, the Huskies began the regular season with non-conference wins over [[America East Conference|America East]] teams, [[2010–11 Stony Brook Seawolves men's basketball team|Stony Brook]] and [[2010–11 Vermont Catamounts men's basketball team|Vermont]]. In the win against Vermont, Kemba Walker tied a UConn XL Center record by scoring 42 points.{{cite news|last=Borges|first=David|title=UCONN MEN'S BASKETBALL: They'll Rememba Kemba; Walker matches record with 42 in win over Vermont|url=http://www.nhregister.com/articles/2010/11/17/sports/doc4ce48a9883057536908867.txt|access-date=May 29, 2011|newspaper=New Haven Register|date=November 17, 2011}}
The team next travelled to Hawaii to play in the 2010 [[Maui Invitational Tournament]]. They last participated in the tournament in 2005, when they won the championship. To open the current tournament, they played [[2010–11 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]]. Walker scored 29 of his 31 points in the second in the 83–79 win.{{cite web|title=UConn's Kemba Walker scores 29 of his 31 points in second half|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=303260041|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120709020536/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=303260041|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 9, 2012|publisher=ESPN|date=November 22, 2010|access-date=May 29, 2011}} The victory meant they would match up with [[2010–11 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]], who was ranked No. 2 in the AP poll at the time. Walker scored 30 points, the third straight game that he eclipsed the 30 point mark, as the Huskies won 70–67.{{cite web|title=Kemba Walker's 30 points power Huskies past second-ranked Spartans|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=303270127|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715105835/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=303270127|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 15, 2012|publisher=ESPN|date=November 23, 2010|access-date=May 29, 2011}} In the championship game, the Huskies outscored [[2010–11 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] 21–2 at the end of the first half, and defeated the Wildcats, 84–67.{{cite news|last=Marshall|first=John|title=Walker leads UConn to Maui title over Kentucky|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recap?gid=201011240129|access-date=May 29, 2011|agency=Associated Press|date=November 25, 2010}} Walker, who scored 29 points in the final, was named the tournament's Most Valuable Player. His 90 points was just three points short of the Maui Invitational record.{{cite web|title=Kemba Walker scores 29 points as UConn upsets Kentucky, wins Maui Invitational|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=303280096|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101129041316/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=303280096|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 29, 2010|publisher=ESPN|date=November 25, 2010|access-date=May 29, 2011}} [[Alex Oriakhi]] was also named to the all-tournament team. == Postseason == The Huskies entered the [[2011 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] as the No. 9 seed, just missing the cut to earn a First round bye. UConn went on to win five games in five consecutive days to earn the Tournament Championship, and an automatic bid into the [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. In the Big East tournament, UConn defeated four teams ranked in the Associated Press Top 25.{{cite web|title=2011 NCAA Men's Basketball Rankings – AP Top 25 Week 18 (Mar. 7)|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/rankings/_/year/2011/poll/1/week/18/seasontype/2|publisher=ESPN|access-date=October 21, 2011|date=March 7, 2011}} UConn received a No. 3 seed in the NCAA Tournament's West Region. They continued their winning streak all the way to the National Championship, finishing the season with eleven consecutive wins.
